newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt rises, yawns at FOMC result.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt rises, yawns at FOMC result.

text.p: The emerging debt market rose on Wednesday, but it largely shrugged off the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave short-term interest rates unchanged, traders said.
Prices edged off their highs briefly as dealers unwound long positions to take profits after the Federal Open Market Committee ended its two-day policy meeting, they said.
"Ten minutes before the (FOMC) announcement, the market started to sell off," one trader said.
But dealers quickly set new long positions and prices rebounded to their pre-announcement levels, he said.
Volume generally remained thin, with almost no retail involvement, traders said.
Spreads over U.S. Treasuries tightened for most issues, especially those of Ecuador and Bulgaria.

Ecuador PDIs ECPDI=RR rose 3/4 to 66-3/4, tightening about 17 basis points. Traders said Ecuador continued to bounce back from last week's declines, but they added that very little of the country's paper actually traded hands.
Bulgaria IABs BGLFTH11=RR climbed 5/8 to 73-3/4, narrowing about 21 basis points, on optimism over the country's economic reforms, traders said.
"People are starting to realize that Bulgaria is doing this for real," said Eric Nielsen, vice president and a senior economist at Goldman Sachs.
On Tuesday, Bulgaria initiated a currency board system to peg the lev to the mark.
Major Latin American issues rose less markedly. Brazil "C" bonds BR8D14=RR were up 1/4 at 81-1/4, Argentina FRBs ARFLC05=RR climbed 1/8 to 94-1/4 and Mexico pars MX625L19=RR rose 1/4 to 78-1/2.
Fixed income investors will pore over the monthly U.S. employment report on Friday. Economists expect it to show 222,000 additional jobs were created last month, compared with 138,000 in May.
"I think people are well-positioned for tomorrow's number, and if it is a friendly number for Treasuries, we'll continue to tighten," said one trader.
